No installed browser lets another app open a private tab. Most Chromium browsers, including Vanadium, refuse this by design; Firefox and its forks allow it.
Opened normally: no installed browser accepts a private-tab request.

%1$s does not let another app open a private tab. Chromium browsers refuse this by design; Firefox and its forks allow it, and Firefox Focus is always private. You can change the browser this app uses in Settings.
Link to the Reddit app blocked.
External links are turned off in Settings.
No browser installed to open this link.
This app clears cookies when it closes, so a signed-in session will not survive. Keep the session to stay signed in, or sign in for this run only.
Check your connection and pull down to retry. If this keeps happening on one page, try turning the blocklist down, or turning off bundle blocking, in Settings.
This setting is read when the page viewer is created, so it takes effect the next time the app starts.
%1$s\n\nSaved, but not in effect until the app is restarted.

Adds "Why is this blank?" and "Save page HTML" to the menu, and allows this app\'s page to be inspected over adb from a computer. Off by default: it defines a variable a page could look for, and it opens the viewer to a debugger. Turn it on to investigate something, then turn it off.
Page saved. Session identifiers were scrubbed.
Remove app prompts and the 18+ wall
Hides Reddit\'s "open in app" takeover and the age wall it uses to push the app, and unblurs the content behind them.
Show adult content without tapping through

Presses Reddit\'s own "View NSFW content" button for you once the page has loaded, rather than editing the page. If a post ever comes up blank, turn this off: the button comes back and the 18+ wall stays gone.
Block the prompt code from loading
Refuses Reddit\'s app-promotion scripts at the network, so the overlays are never built rather than removed afterwards. Turn off if part of the site stops working.
Clear cookies, storage and cache when the app closes. Turning this off is what lets a sign-in persist.

Presses Reddit\'s own "Yes, I\'m Over 18" button when it appears, and seeds the cookie it sets. That button also records the dismissal server-side, which is what makes Reddit send an adult-flagged post\'s media at all — a cookie alone does not. Turn this off and you will be asked by Reddit instead.
Open off-site links in a browser
Off keeps every non-Reddit link from leaving the app at all.
Which browser this app hands non-Reddit links to. Independent of your system default, so you can keep one browser for everyday use and send links from here somewhere disposable.
%1$s is no longer installed — using the system default. Pick another in Settings.

Only applies when the browser above has both modes. Firefox and its forks honour a private-tab request from another app; Chromium browsers, including Vanadium, refuse it, and the app says so rather than opening a normal tab and calling it private. A browser that is always private, like Firefox Focus, never asks.
